## Plan: show a friendly message when no invoices match

**Before** — `app/invoices/page.tsx` renders its `<table>` unconditionally, so a list with no rows would render a header row over an empty body.

**After** — the table markup moves verbatim into a new server component `app/invoices/InvoiceTable.tsx` that takes `invoices: readonly Invoice[]`. When that list is empty it renders

> No invoices match this filter

instead of the table; otherwise it renders exactly the table that is there today. The page passes `listInvoices()` straight through, so with the seeded data nothing a user sees changes.

### One thing worth saying plainly

This app has no status filter. `listInvoices()` returns a hard-coded five-invoice array (`lib/invoices.ts`), so the empty state is not reachable through the UI today — I read the filter in your request as an example of *when* the table would be empty, not as something to build. **Adding a filter is a separate work item and is not part of this one** — it is already filed as #27. The empty state is checked by temporarily emptying the seed and loading the page in a browser, and by a unit test.

The conditional goes in a small extracted component rather than inline in the page, because the page's own test can only ever produce the seeded non-empty list — testing the empty branch in place would need to mock `lib/invoices`, which this repo does not do anywhere. A component taking the list as a prop is testable both ways with the pattern `components/ExportButton.test.tsx` already uses. It sits beside the page rather than in `components/`, which the feature map reserves for UI more than one feature needs.

### Files the build may touch

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `app/invoices/InvoiceTable.tsx` | new — the table, plus the empty-state paragraph |
| `app/invoices/InvoiceTable.test.tsx` | new — empty-list and two-invoice cases |
| `app/invoices/page.tsx` | renders `<InvoiceTable invoices={invoices} />` in place of the table |

`app/invoices/page.test.tsx` is **not** modified: the rendered DOM is unchanged, so its two assertions still hold. No new dependency, nothing under `lib/` or `components/`.

### Acceptance checks

1. With the seeded data untouched, `/invoices` still lists all five invoices, still reads "Export 3 invoices as CSV" and "Total sent: $1,497.50", and the text "No invoices match this filter" appears nowhere.
2. With `INVOICES` temporarily set to `[]` and the app rebuilt, `/invoices` shows "No invoices match this filter" and no `<table>` element at all — then the seed is restored and the page is back to five rows. (A scratch edit; it is not committed.)
3. `npm test` — the new case rendering `<InvoiceTable invoices={[]} />` finds that exact text and no table element.
4. `npm test` — the new case rendering two invoices finds three rows (header plus one each), both ids, and no empty-state text, so the extraction did not change the table.
5. `npm test -- --coverage`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` all exit 0, the existing suite passes unmodified, and both changed `app/invoices` files report 100% of lines.

### What I checked while planning

- `./InvoiceTable.js` (the `.js` suffix the test files use) **fails `next build`** with "Module not found", even though `tsc` and vitest accept it — so the page imports it extensionless. Verified by building a probe both ways.
- `app/invoices/page.tsx` is already at 100% line coverage via `app/invoices/page.test.tsx`; the sandbox manifest's note that the page components are at 0% and the suite is 21 tests in 3 files is out of date (it is 26 tests in 4 files).
- A probe of the planned shape — sibling component plus colocated test — reaches 100% coverage with the suite green, which keeps the 80% diff-coverage gate satisfied.
- `formatAmount` has to come out of the page's import once the table leaves, or `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` fails the lint.

All probe files were deleted; the working tree is unchanged.
